title: Predicted line-ups for every Premier League team in Matchweek 4
body:
Football writer Ben Bloom has predicted how all 20 Premier League clubs could line up in Matchweek 4.

See: Injury updates for every club and player
See: Who's suspended or close to a ban?

Aston Villa v Nottingham Forest predicted line-ups

Aston Villa: Muscle soreness meant Matty Cash missed the midweek UEFA Champions League game, with Aaron Wan-Bissaka coming in at right-back. Unai Emery confirmed he will make a late check on whether Cash can return here. Johan Manzambi could make the bench after recovering from a knee problem, while Emery suggested fellow new signing Ibrahim Mbaye needs to “be patient” in his desire for minutes. Joao Gomes is still suspended.

See: Villa team news

Nott'm Forest: Ibrahim Sangare trained ahead of the Spurs game last weekend, but failed to make the matchday squad, which meant Xaver Schlager retained his place. Oliver Glasner said Nicolo Savona is his only absentee, which suggests he has a decision to make between Sangare, Schlager and James McAtee in central midfield. Daniel Munoz will hope to start after making his debut off the bench last time out, while Liam Delap should retain his spot up front. Goals have been scant, so there is a chance Igor Jesus, Callum Hudson-Odoi or Chris Wood receive the nod. Ousmane Diomande has yet to force his way in at the back.

See: Nott'm Forest team news

AFC Bournemouth v Brentford predicted line-ups

Bournemouth: The Cherries have no new injuries to add to their pre-existing absent quartet - Eli Kroupi, Julian Araujo, Amine Adli and Veljko Milosavljevic - none of whom are expected back within the next month. Marco Rose has made few changes in the league so far, although his side continue to be blighted by conceding late goals. Ryan Christie seized his EFL Cup opportunity in midweek with a hat-trick against Lincoln City. He is an option to replace Tyler Adams in the middle, as is Lewis Cook.

See: Bournemouth team news

Brentford: Nathan Collins has been ruled out until after the international break, which is likely to mean a first Premier League start for Jannik Schuster, who replaced him early last weekend. Jaidon Anthony came on for Dango Ouattara at half-time in that match and may well start here, with neither player yet able to nail down their spot. With Mathias Jensen still out, Yehor Yarmoliuk is another central midfield option.

See: Brentford team news

Chelsea v Hull City predicted line-ups

Chelsea: A number of Chelsea’s fringe players failed to impress in their EFL Cup comeback win against Leeds on Wednesday, so expect a very similar side to that which started against Arsenal last weekend. One potential change is Levi Colwill in for Josh Acheampong, while Malo Gusto and Pep Chavarria are alternative wing-back options. Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra remain out.

See: Chelsea team news

Hull: Hull’s second string failed to impress in the EFL Cup on Tuesday, which should mean a return to the first-choice side that remains unbeaten in three Premier League outings and are yet to concede a goal. Sergej Jakirovic suggested Jon Egan and Lewie Coyle are both fine, while Tim Iroegbunam, Brooke Norton-Cuffy and Paddy McNair are all expected to return to training in time for this. Matt Crooks could challenge Lucas Gourna-Douath for a place in central midfield.

Crystal Palace v Ipswich Town predicted line-ups

Crystal Palace: Jorgen Strand Larsen scored twice in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, strengthening his claim to be restored up front instead of Eddie Nketiah, who was forced off at half-time last weekend and faces a late fitness test. Quentin Timber was thrown straight into action after joining on deadline day, and will hope to retain his central midfield spot. Daichi Kamada was used higher up the pitch last weekend in one of the two No 10 places. Dario Osorio is a potential option to replace him, or Nketiah could drop deeper if fit.

See: Palace team news

Ipswich: Few changes are expected despite defeat last weekend, although Zian Flemming is pushing for a start ahead of Emersonn, with Gary O’Neil suggesting the forward will play a “big part” here. Jaden Philogene and Azor Matusiwa are both ready for minutes after injuries, but bench spots appear likely. So far, O’Neil has been content to deploy Dara O’Shea at right-back rather than in central defence.

Liverpool v Fulham predicted line-ups

Liverpool: Andoni Iraola confirmed Bradley Barcola’s midweek departure after an hour of UEFA Champions League action was due to cramp, adding “he should be available if everything goes normal”. Cody Gakpo missed that game and Iraola said “we will see” if he returns this weekend or next. Assuming Barcola is fit enough for his first Premier League start, but Gakpo is not, it should mean Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha battling for the other winger spot, unless Jeremie Frimpong is reassigned. Frimpong seems to have lost his right-back place to Ronald Araujo, while Ryan Gravenberch has not started since the opening day of the season.

See: Liverpool team news

Fulham: Alvaro Arbeloa has seen his new Fulham side lose all three of his Premier League games in charge. Shea Charles was handed a first start last time out and will expect to retain his spot. There is a fair chance he is partnered by Sander Berge in the middle, with Alex Iwobi pushed higher up the pitch and Oscar Bobb making way. Emile Smith-Rowe, Ryan Sessegnon and Kevin will be eager to prove their worth if handed an opportunity.

See: Fulham team news

Tottenham Hotspur v Everton predicted line-ups

Spurs: No sooner had he returned to competitive action than Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an injury that will see him out for a couple of months. Mathys Tel looks set to retain his starting spot on the left, assuming Mohammed Kudus is not deemed ready to start (Roberto De Zerbi said he is “very close” to doing so). Conor Gallagher filled the No 10 role last weekend, but might be replaced by Mateus Fernandes, or else Omar Marmoush could drop back with Dominic Solanke starting up top. James Maddison is available after a shoulder issue, while Andy Robertson can challenge Destiny Udogie at left-back.

See: Spurs team news

Everton: David Moyes hinted that Jack Grealish could be in line for his first start of the season, suggesting “playing game time helps” the Man City loanee as he looks to get up to speed. If Grealish starts on the left wing, it may well see Tyrique George move to the opposite flank, with Brennan Johnson dropping out of the XI. James Garner has been passed fit after suffering cramp, although Hayden Hackney provides an alternative option. Ainsley Maitland-Niles could challenge Merlin Rohl for the right-back spot following his spectacular goalscoring debut last weekend.

See: Everton team news

Sunderland v Arsenal predicted line-ups

Sunderland: Kevin Danso started at centre-back last weekend, with Nordi Mukiele shifting to right-back and Thomas Meunier moving into midfield. Sunderland then fielded an entirely different XI in the EFL Cup on Tuesday night, and Regis Le Bris suggested it is “possible” that some of those players could make their way into his Premier League starting side. Primary among them might be left-back Dayann Methalie, winger Malick Fofana and the versatile Trai Hume. Le Bris could also opt for three/five at the back, although that does not necessarily require any personnel changes.

See: Sunderland team news

Arsenal: After making a couple of changes for UEFA Champions League action on Wednesday, expect Mikel Arteta to revert to the same XI he fielded against Chelsea in Arsenal’s last Premier League outing. The manager suggested there were no new injuries to report, with Cristhian Mosquera and Jurrien Timber potentially in contention for this, although bench spots look likely at most. Christos Tzolis will hope to keep Eberechi Eze out, while Kai Havertz will come back in for Viktor Gyokeres. The question of when Bruno Guimaraes makes his way into the starting XI remains.

See: Arsenal team news

Coventry City v Brighton & Hove Albion predicted line-ups

Coventry: It has been a tricky Premier League return for Coventry, who have no points and zero goals so far, but they did not disgrace themselves in defeat at Manchester City last weekend when they switched to a back three. It will be interesting to see if Frank Lampard sticks with that formation, which saw Ethan Pinnock make his first start since joining the club. There is plenty of competition for the two No 10 spots with Jack Rudoni, Ephron Mason-Clark, Brandon Thomas-Asante and Loum Tchaouna all in contention. Frank Onyeka will hope to keep Caleb Yirenkyi out in central midfield unless a return to a back four opens up another spot in the middle.

See: Coventry team news

Brighton: Brighton took an hour to get going against Leeds last weekend, but did eventually produce some good football without making personnel changes off the bench, so Fabian Hurzeler could well stick with the same XI given his medium to long-term attacking absentees. Georginio Rutter “is hopefully available” after missing the last two games with a foot problem, while deadline-day arrival Femi Azeez will “hopefully be an option” having arrived from Millwall with a minor hamstring issue. Fellow new boy Zadok Yohanna is out. If Hurzeler is looking for changes, Costinha could come it at right-back with Ferdi Kadioglu switching sides, while Rutter would replace Charalampos Kostoulas if deemed fit enough.

See: Brighton team news

Manchester United v Manchester City predicted line-ups

Man Utd: Michael Carrick’s big decision is whether to lead his attack with Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko, or start both of them. Sesko has scored twice in as many games, and Carrick might be tempted to keep the same front four from Thursday’s UEFA Champions League win over Sabah, which would see Marcus Rashford lose his place and Cunha play on the left. It’s a tough one to call. Luke Shaw missed that midweek game, with Patrick Dorgu filling in at left-back. He can do so again if required.

See: Man Utd team news

Man City: Enzo Maresca confirmed Nico O’Reilly is “100 per cent available” after withdrawing from the starting line-up shortly before kick-off last weekend, and then skipping UEFA Champions League duty on Tuesday. His absence saw Enzo Fernandez start both games, partnered in the middle by Elliot Anderson for one, and Ayyoub Bouaddi for the other. If O’Reilly does return, it looks more likely to be at left-back in place of Josko Gvardiol than in midfield, while it is a close call between Matheus Nunes and Abdukodir Khusanov on the other side. It looks like a straight scrap between Iliman Ndiaye and Phil Foden for the final attacking spot.

See: Man City team news

Leeds United v Newcastle United predicted line-ups

Leeds: Jaka Bijol was the defender to miss out last weekend, with Nico Elvedi starting in place of the injured Joe Rodon, and James Justin shifting to centre-back. Those three fit players will likely contest two places here. Further forward, Harry Wilson and Brenden Aaronson were both substitutes in that match, with Ao Tanaka and Noah Okafor favoured instead. Daniel Farke faces the same selection decisions here as there is no space for all four of those attackers.

See: Leeds team news

Newcastle: Tino Livramento played the entire second half in midweek EFL Cup action at Millwall, but a start would be a big call given how long he was out for. Matthias Jaissle suggested right-back Amar Dedic “felt a little bit of something with his hamstring” when coming off in that match though, so there could be a hole to fill, but the manager added that it “does not look too serious”. Lewis Miley would be an option to fill in there if needed, with Sean Steur or Jacob Ramsey coming into central midfield. Matias Fernandez-Pardo is yet to start; when he does, expect Yoane Wissa to potentially drop into the No 10 role.

See: Newcastle team news
